newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shrs off on thin trade as eyes on U.S. rates.
newsitem.headline: Lima shrs off on thin trade as eyes on U.S. rates.

text.p: The Lima Stock Exchange dipped slightly Monday in thin trading as investors waited nervously for the U.S. Federal Reserve to announce its decision on interest rates, brokers said.
They predicted a similar tendency for Tuesday.
"Nobody wants to take a risk," said Pablo Navarro, of Fortuna brokerage.
With a 60 percent participation of foreign capital, events outside Peru often affect the market as much or more as domestic developments.
The general index fell 0.17 percent to 1,662.03 points and the blue-chip selective index was off 0.39 percent to 2,394.51.
Trading volume was a moderate 20.4 million soles ($7.8 million) as 22 shares fell, 24 rose and 36 remained flat.

Biggest losers included electricity generator Edegel, off 3.1 percent to 1.22 soles, benchmark Telefonica del Peru, which lost 1.5 percent to 5.90 soles, and Banco de Credito, down 0.9 percent to 4.42 soles.
Among stocks that advanced were miner Milpo, up 6.39 percent to 20.80 soles, and fellow miner Morococha, which gained 1.81 percent to 2.24 soles.

"The polymetallic mining shares are showing an enviable strength thanks to their perspectives. They are currently the most healthy alternative due to the volatility of the other stocks," said Hernando Pastor, of T&J brokerage.
He added that imminent first quarter corporate results, expected to be positive, should boost the market.
